_about: Parameters of the behaviour layer's segments and features (agentcake/detect/segment.py and features.py). The values are our lab's, unchanged (the behaviour lab's labcore.py, 2026-11-11); the missing-data variant is our PostHog study's (cake-ph-eval/phcore.py, 2026-11-12).

segments._about: window_ms: length of the fixed windows. One segment per action: events of a typing or scroll burst are at most gap_ms apart; pointer moves within scroll_move_ms of a scroll burst belong to it (moves made while scrolling); a pause longer than approach_pause_ms between pointer moves ends the approach to the next action.

features._about: min_duration_s: shortest segment length for move_rate. before_click_ms, hover_ms, down_ms: how far before a click to look for mouse moves, a mouseover on the same target and the mousedown. min_path_moves: trusted moves needed for the path features; cv_min_speeds and jerk_min_speeds: speeds needed for speed_cv and jerk_any; jerk_speed_step: a speed change above this (px/ms) is a jerk. wheel_after_ms: a scroll this soon after a wheel or key event came from it, as does one while a finger or a button is held down or this soon after its release (after agent-detector's scroll drivers, MIT). keydown_before_ms: typed text this soon after a keydown came from it. typed_input_types: the input types that are typed text, the only ones input_no_keydown reads (after agent-detector's insertWithoutKeys, MIT): a paste, an autofill or a correction (insertReplacementText), a drop and an input method's composition (isComposing) change a field without a keydown, and humans make them; nor does it read a session where a finger or a pen gave input. metronome_min_keys and burst_min_keys: keydowns needed for key_iv_cv and key_burst; key_burst_ms: keydowns closer than this are a burst. click_lt_px: a click closer than this to the centre of its target. offset_min_events: pointer events with screen positions needed on the page for screen_offset_jump. screen_eq_min_positions: screen_eq_client counts screen positions equal to page positions only when they were equal at this many different places in the session (after bot-signal's cdp-input-coordinate-leak, MIT): one place is a window in the screen's corner. double_click_box_px: a mouse click repeats the previous mouse click in place when it lands inside the square of this side centred on that click and every mousemove between the two stayed inside it too: the square within which a browser counts a second click as one at the same place (Chromium's MouseEvent::IsRepeatedClickEvent: 4 by 4 px, Windows' default double-click rectangle, SM_CXDOUBLECLK by SM_CYDOUBLECLK). Such a click shows no approach of its own, the pointer being on the spot already: a person paging through pictures or pressing a calendar's arrow again, an agent pressing a button twice, a label passing its click to its input. So moves_before_click leaves it out, as do the teleport clicks and the timeline's pointer features (behavior_model.json); where it lands on its target (the click centre features) is still read. No time limit: however long the pointer rests on the spot, it makes no new approach.

unobservable._about: Features an rrweb-only recording cannot measure (no keydown, no wheel, no screenX/Y, no movementX/Y). Without raw input they are null (no data), never 0: the missing-data variant.
